{"world_model":"W6 model after E048. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step, E043/E047). Tip E036: 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Same-commit reruns read 0.7525, 0.7497 and 0.7544 (E038, E043, E047), so 3-seed noise is ±0.2 pp. The population mean is about 0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the 0.75 bar. Time noise is ±0.04 s, with build-to-build drift of up to ~0.05 s.

Mechanisms:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, at about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch or sample cuts (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048) trade at dial-like rates and are not free. E048's 95% selection saved 0.33 s (more than expected) for −0.1 pp, in line with that rate.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036, E046), because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. E046 saved ~0.24 s at about −0.1 pp. Late freezes are neutral and early ones are not (E037's cliff).
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe is near a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by −0.1 pp.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047), so I076's ceiling is ~1–1.5%.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Activation swaps: the fused kernels are bytes-bound, so GELU→ReLU should save little time (~1–2%) and cost accuracy.

Misses: truncation and selection savings beat my estimates (E037, E041, E046, E048), and accuracy swung ±0.3 pp on identical code. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges, treat 3-seed differences below 0.3 pp as noise, and expect step-count cuts to save slightly more time than linear scaling suggests.

Unsure: the true tip mean (0.752 ± 0.1), selection bias, transfer to the PCIe judge, and whether the group-2 freeze can extend past 10%.

Headroom: any time-trading step needs an accuracy source. W6 model after E048. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step, E043/E047). Tip E036: 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Same-commit reruns read 0.7525, 0.7497 and 0.7544 (E038, E043, E047), so 3-seed noise is ±0.2 pp. The population mean is about 0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the 0.75 bar. Time noise is ±0.04 s, with build-to-build drift of up to ~0.05 s.

Mechanisms:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, at about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch or sample cuts (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048) trade at dial-like rates and are not free. E048's 95% selection saved 0.33 s (more than expected) for −0.1 pp, in line with that rate.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036, E046), because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. E046 saved ~0.24 s at about −0.1 pp. Late freezes are neutral and early ones are not (E037's cliff).
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe is near a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by −0.1 pp.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047), so I076's ceiling is ~1–1.5%.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Activation swaps: the fused kernels are bytes-bound, so GELU→ReLU should save little time (~1–2%) and cost accuracy.

Misses: truncation and selection savings beat my estimates (E037, E041, E046, E048), and accuracy swung ±0.3 pp on identical code. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges, treat 3-seed differences below 0.3 pp as noise, and expect step-count cuts to save slightly more time than linear scaling suggests.

Unsure: the true tip mean (0.752 ± 0.1), selection bias, transfer to the PCIe judge, and whether the group-2 freeze can extend past 10%.

Headroom: any time-trading step needs an accuracy source. A +0.25 epoch top-up buys ~0.1 pp for ~0.1 s.

forecasts.reason: The group-2 freeze saves ~0.2 s and the top-up adds ~0.1 s, so net time is about −3%. Accuracy is roughly neutral within noise.
A systems-only change gives about 1% at best, which is near the noise floor. Accuracy is unchanged apart from rebuild noise.
The kernels are bytes-bound, so ReLU saves little time. ReLU likely loses a little accuracy, and the 3% time gate is probably missed.

cruxes: What is the true unselected population mean of the tip (seeds 13–32, same build)? It sets how much accuracy margin is left to trade for time.
Does the group-2 freeze stay neutral when combined with an epoch top-up, and can the freeze dose extend beyond 10% of steps?
Are the fused BN/activation kernels purely bytes-bound? If so, activation swaps do nothing, and only removing activation layers or bytes would help.
